3. <u>Transmission and Pipelines</u>. Electrical power lines and radio communication lines will involve the use of supports, the bases of which will extend into the surface snow and uppermost firn. In addition, fuel lines from fuel bladders to points of use will impose a local disturbance on the snow surface. Power lines, supports, fuel bladders and fuel lines will be removed when the camp is closed.
4. <u>Water Well Emplacement</u>. If water for domestic and scientific use is obtained by melting in the upper part of the ice, there will be a cased hole through the snow and firn, and a void will be created where this ice is melted and the water removed. The heat exchanger and pump will be recovered; however, it may not prove possible to recover the casing.
5. <u>Microbial Introductions</u>. No alien species of organisms beyond those normally carried by man will be introduced. These microorganisms will be associated largely with the immediate vicinity of the camp and scientific operations. Routine monitoring for enteric organisms in the food and water supplies as well as in the snow will be carried out throughout the RISP program.
6. <u>Burning</u>. Combustible wastes such as wood, wood products, and paper will be incinerated. Smoke generated will deposit particulate matter downwind. Ash will remain <u>in situ</u>. Neither can be considered a significant detriment to the local environment and will be quickly buried
